00:12:17 *🔄 AGA involves downstream fibrosis/inflammation beyond DHT.*
00:13:14 *💉 Botox (TGF-beta proxy) increases hair density in AGA studies.*
00:13:41 *📊 Zhao study: Botox alone matches Botox + finasteride for hair density gains.*

videos.title: Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia: Understanding and Treating This Hair Loss Condition
videos.description:
In this video, Dr. Nina Otberg provides an in-depth explanation of frontal fibrosing alopecia (FFA), a scarring hair loss condition that primarily affects women during and after menopause, but can also impact men. Dr. Otberg discusses the causes, symptoms, and progression of FFA, as well as the latest treatment options available. Whether you’re experiencing symptoms yourself or want to learn more about this condition, this video offers valuable insights into managing and treating frontal fibrosing alopecia effectively.

Key topics covered in this video:

What is frontal fibrosing alopecia (FFA)?
Who is affected by FFA, and why it commonly occurs in postmenopausal women.
The symptoms and progression of FFA.
Treatment options, including medical and surgical approaches.
Advice on managing the condition and preserving hair health.

New research into androgenetic alopecia suggests something may be happening inside miniaturizing hair follicles that DHT and conventional hair loss treatments do not fully address.

In this video you will learn:

🔹 The hidden scalp change researchers found as hair follicles became more miniaturized
🔹 Why some follicles may eventually stop responding to minoxidil and finasteride
🔹 What scientists discovered inside a critical regenerative region of the hair follicle
🔹 Why treating hair loss later may be very different from treating it early

I EXPOSED the hair loss industry in this viral hair health video (you need to see it) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BlPb46W0Fm4

Hair loss is often explained through DHT and follicle miniaturization alone. But emerging research into fibrosis raises a much bigger question about what happens to the scalp environment as androgenetic alopecia progresses.

videos.title: Managing Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia discussion - David Saceda, MD, PhD & Sam Lam
videos.description:
Learn more about Dr. Saceda and the ISHRS 33rd World Congress here: https://33rdannual.org/dr-saceda/

We’re excited to have Dr. David Saceda join us as a featured guest speaker at the ISHRS 33rd World Congress in Berlin, where he will present on: “Managing Frontal Fibrosing Alopecia.”

Dr. Saceda is a hair transplant surgeon and dermatologist who works in the Hair Disorders Unit of Hospital Ramón y Cajal and Grupo de Dermatología Pedro Jaén in Madrid, Spain, and also teaches at the University of Alcalá.

In this short video, he joins Dr. Sam Lam, Chair of the Congress, to give a preview of his presentation on one of the most common hair disorders, FFA, an autoimmune condition that, according to Dr. Saceda, has seen an increase in cases over the past decade.
